- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or trending down, adjust upward by 2–5% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- If recent auction supply events are frequent (≥15/30d) and model forecast is rising, cap upward momentum at 1–3% above recent peak to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome spikes sharply after a flat forecast, apply a “lag correction” — add 1–3% to forecast for next period to account for delayed reaction.
- When official event net is bearish (net < -10) and sentiment is neutral or bearish, reduce forecast by 1–3% to reflect policy/supply pressure.
- If model forecast is flat over 5+ days and true outcome shows mean reversion, apply a “reversion bias” — adjust downward 1–2% per period if sentiment is weak.
- For periods with high event count and low sentiment, model should not over-forecast — use 1–2% floor below recent high to avoid overconfidence in supply-driven volatility.
